cincinnati-ballet-center-for-dance: The Ballet identifies an Everybody Restroom on the first floor with a shower stall it describes as accessible. It does not specify an adult changing table or transfer equipment.
The Everybody Restroom on the first floor is both accessible and includes a shower stall that is accessible.

For CB Moves for Parkinson’s, visitors signing up in person are asked to arrive 15 minutes early for check-in and waivers. The online schedule links to Mindbody for reservations, payment and schedule or capacity changes.

The schedule below updates regularly and offers direct access to Cincinnati Ballet's Mindbody site. Through Mindbody you can: Reserve your space in class Purchase a class Create and manage your account Check changes to the schedule or class capacities If you prefer to sign-up in person, please arrive 15 minutes early to check in and complete any waivers prior to class.
CB Moves for Parkinson’s costs $10 per class and includes a companion participant at no additional charge. Confirm the current class schedule and space before travelling.
All classes are $10 and include a companion participant (if desired) at no additional charge.

CB Moves for Parkinson’s participants may dance seated, use a chair or barre for balance, modify steps and take breaks. Standing and unaided movement across the floor are not required; this is class participation guidance, not a promise of transfer or personal-care assistance.

At any point, dancers may opt to use a chair or the barre for balance instead of standing on their own, or to sit down in a chair and dance seated. Additionally, dancers are encouraged to modify steps as necessary to participate at their own level, and take breaks as needed. Standing and unaided movement across the floor is not necessary to participate. We have had many students successfully navigate class using wheelchairs, walkers, canes, and other mobility devices.

For the Ballet’s sensory-friendly performances, house lights remain at half brightness, volunteers are stationed in the audience, lobby and outside, and quiet areas are designated in the lobby. Confirm the performance location; this is not an everyday quiet-room promise at the Center for Dance.
House lights remain at half brightness during the entire performance.
Volunteers are stationed throughout the audience, lobby and outside the venue to assist audience members. Quiet areas are designated in the lobby.
cincinnati-observatory: The Mitchel building’s front entrance has five steps with handrails. The published alternative is the side ramp to the main floor; reaching the dome and eyepiece involves additional steps.
The front entrance has 5 steps with handrails. There is an ADA compliant ramp to the side entrance which brings visitors into the main floor with access to the classroom, lobby, and restrooms.
The Telescope Dome Room is only accessible by 5 steps with handrails on both sides. As noted above, reaching the telescope eyepiece usually involves additional steps.
cincinnati-playhouse-in-the-park: The Rouse Theatre doors are on the first lobby level. The elevator serves the balcony and front orchestra rows, and also reaches the Rosenthal Shelterhouse Theatre on the second floor. Arrange a specific seat and route when booking.

The doors are on the first level of the lobby, which means that all patrons can access the new theatre on the same level where they enter the building, only using the elevator for seats in the balcony section or front rows. The elevator can also be used to access the Rosenthal Shelterhouse Theatre, which will remain in its second-floor location.
The elevator for the new building will take patrons up to the balcony or down to the front rows of the orchestra section.

For hearing-enhancement receivers, the Playhouse directs visitors to the house manager. Both theaters have hearing loops for T-coil or Telecoil hearing aids and cochlear implants; confirm how to collect and use any receiver you need.

Moe and Jack's Place - The Rouse Theatre and the Rosenthal Shelterhouse Theatre both have a hearing loop system which works with existing T-Coil or Telecoil enabled hearing aids or cochlear implants. In addition, hearing enhancement receivers providing volume enhancement to patrons with hearing impairment are available. Please see the house manager for more information.

Audio description is free on the listed performance dates. Trained volunteers describe visual action through the hearing-enhancement system, avoiding dialogue; show and actor information is also shared before the performance and at intermission.

Trained volunteers describe the visual elements of the production via a hearing enhancement system, allowing patrons to hear dialogue, music and other sound effects. The description is timed to avoid interfering with dialogue. Before the show and during intermission, show and actor information are shared. This service is free. Please see dates below.
cincinnati-music-hall: The drop-off lane is on Elm Street near the Box Office and wheelchair entrance at 1241 Elm Street. Music Hall does not own or manage the listed parking facilities, so confirm availability and rates with the operator.

A convenient drop-off lane is located in front of Music Hall on Elm Street, near the Box Office and wheelchair-accessible entrance (1241 Elm Street). NOTE: Music Hall does not own or manage the parking facilities listed below. Parking rates are subject to change and are posted at each lot.

For Springer Hall performances, staff can provide access to an area for nursing. Ask a staff member for its location and entry; this page does not describe equipment or a dedicated room available for every event.
Our Springer Hall performances do offer an area for nursing mothers. Please speak to a staff member for assistance and access to the location.

Music Hall’s access page asks visitors bringing a service animal to notify their ticketing representative when buying tickets and says animals should remain leashed or harnessed. Confirm any seating arrangements with the venue.

Service animals are always welcome and should remain on a leash or in a harness at all times. If you plan to bring a service animal to an event, please notify your ticketing services representative at the time of purchase.
Music Hall entry generally begins one to one-and-a-half hours before an event, depending on the performance’s policy. Anyone who leaves the building must repeat safety screening to re-enter.
MUSIC HALL: You may enter Music Hall anytime beginning one to one-and-one-half hours before the start of an event, depending on the policies of the performance.
Anyone who leaves either building at any time will need to repeat the safety screening to re-enter the venues.

The tours FAQ says no bathroom breaks are scheduled and recommends arriving 15 minutes early. Outdoor-tour guests are directed to Washington Park’s Race Street restroom because indoor Music Hall restrooms are not available for that tour.

We do not stop at any restrooms or take any bathroom breaks during any of our tours. You are encouraged to arrive 15 minutes before your start time to use the restrooms. Outdoor building tour guests should visit the park's public restroom on the Race Street side of Washington Park as indoor restrooms will not be available.

Indoor Music Hall tours offer brief opportunities to sit; tell the organizer when booking if minimal stairs would be a problem. Outdoor tours have no sitting opportunities and expect participants to remain on their feet without assistance. The FAQ also says tour paths accommodate walkers and wheelchairs; confirm your route and support needs.

Indoor building tours provide some opportunities to sit briefly. Our indoor tour is completely ADA accessible however, please let us know at the time of your reservation if you have trouble climbing minimal stairs.

Our outdoor building tour is a 360 degree walk around the building which is about the length and width of a football field. The route does not go up or down any stairs or hills. Tour guests are expected to stay on their feet the whole time without assistance and there are no opportunities to sit along the tour route.
Cincinnati Music Hall is 100% ADA compliant and the tour path accommodates those in walkers and wheelchairs.

The tours FAQ describes indoor tours year-round and outdoor tours May–October. It recommends advance tickets because spaces are limited; same-day purchase depends on space. Reservations must be paid for in advance. Confirm the current tour calendar before travelling.

Indoor tours are offered year round while outdoor tours are only offered May - October. It is recommended that guests make a reservation and buy tickets in advance through the Cincinnati Arts Association or Music Hall box offices as space is limited. If space is available, tickets can be purchased the day of the tour. All reservations must be paid for in advance.
